{'text': '紐約市市長索赫蘭·馬姆達尼週日猛烈抨擊國土安全部部長馬克韋恩·穆林，針對他對上週布朗克斯槍擊事件的回應。事件中，聯邦移民執法人員開槍擊中28歲的奧斯卡·貝爾加爾，當時他與自己5歲的孩子同在車內。'}

{'text': '「我認為他們一次又一次地表明，他們視法律為建議。這正是紐約市警察局不會向行駛中的車輛開槍的原因。這正是執法人員理應佩戴可識別標識和制服的原因，」市長在接受MS NOW的雅各布·索博羅夫採訪時說道。'}

{'text': '根據警方公佈的監控錄像，貝爾加爾週四在一個繁忙的社區駕車載著兒子時，數名便衣移民及海關執法局（ICE）特工拔槍逼近他。部分特工戴著面罩，而一名未戴面罩的特工則身穿建築背心、手持步槍。'}

{'text': '槍擊發生時紐約市警察局並不在現場，但警方的隨身攝錄機片段顯示了事後的混亂場面，貝爾加爾受傷躺在街上。這名28歲男子的兒子當時坐在後座目睹了槍擊過程，身體未受傷害。然而，州長 Kathy Hochul（民主黨人）週五表示，這名男孩受到嚴重創傷，至今無法開口說話。'}

{'text': '「你在那段影片以及隨後公佈的影片中可以看到，旁觀者——那些站在外面的人——根本不知道自己在看的是什麼，」馬姆達尼說。「因為在那些畫面中，感覺幾乎像是在看一名大規模槍手，而不是一個自稱代表聯邦機構的人。」'}

{'text': 'ICE尚未公佈槍擊事件本身的影片，但該機構和穆林已搬出他們慣用的一套說法來為這次攻擊行為開脫：聲稱被擊中者是罪犯、將自己的車輛變成對付特工的武器、並把自己和親人置於被槍擊的危險之中。'}

{'text': '「我們當時不知道車內有一名5歲兒童。知道車內有誰的人是奧斯卡，」穆林週日在哥倫比亞廣播公司（CBS）的《面對全國》節目中說道。「作為六個孩子的父親——呃，我是說六個小孩——我絕對不會把自己的孩子置於危險之中。」'}

{'text': '馬姆達尼在槍擊事件後立即作出激烈回應，他表示已分別與穆林和總統當勞倫·特朗普通了電話。市長指出，儘管他表達了對ICE令城市變得更不安全這一層面的憂慮，「讓我不斷感到震驚的是，對於這位部長來說，這些都不是問題。」'}

{'text': '「我們知道，對於這位部長、對於ICE來說，他們天生就把這個國家的許多人視為罪犯，僅僅憑藉他們的長相、居住地、說什麼語言，」馬姆達尼說。「這不是我們治理紐約市的方式，這也不是我們紐約人的作風。」'}

{'text': '警方證實，至少一名ICE特工共開了七槍，其中一槍擊中貝爾加爾的頸部。貝爾加爾的律師表示，他目前仍被聯邦拘留，子彈仍卡在其體內，並且正承受著疼痛。'}

{'text': '馬姆達尼表示，他一直試圖透過談判爭取貝爾加爾獲釋，並將案件移交紐約市警察局處理。據MS NOW報道，特朗普和穆林表示，只有在警方羈押貝爾加爾的情況下他們才會這樣做——而這是市長所不認同的。'}

{'text': '「我問過是根據什麼逮捕令。紐約市並沒有針對貝爾加爾先生的逮捕令，」馬姆達尼說。「當我提出這個問題時，[穆林]開始重複他在新聞發佈會上使用的那套說辭，那套我們知道他們用來描述這個國家許多人的說辭，而這些說辭一旦稍加審查便會不攻自破。」'}

28-year-old female model and daughter-in-law of Tam Wai noodle chain founder Choi Tin-fung was murdered and dismembered in 2023. Her ex-husband Kwong Kong-chi, former father-in-law Kwong Kau, and former brother-in-law Kwong Kong-kit are charged with murder and preventing the lawful burial of a body. Choi's mother Cheung Yin-fa today (the 12th) completed her testimony after being cross-examined by Kwong Kong-chi's defence team.

Kwong Kong-chi's defence today stated he did not oppose the sale of the Kowloon Tong property, and that he had given Choi's mother over HK$370,000 to repay her gambling debts. Choi's mother repeatedly denied this, saying Kwong initially refused to sell the property, and only agreed to urge Kwong Kau to sell after she told him "see you in court"; the funds in question came from selling a car, etc., and it was impossible that Kwong Kong-chi had money to give her. The defence said Choi's mother did not know if Kwong's mainland business was successful, and that she tailored her testimony to match the prosecution. Choi's mother denied this, saying "don't you dare wrong me." Additionally, Choi's mother confirmed her private car was splashed with red paint in February this year. The defence said this was related to her debts; she denied it, saying she was "being framed," and admitted she plays mahjong but considers it entertainment, with amounts "quite small," around "HK$100,000 or HK$80,000 per session."

Related reports:Choi Tin-fung case, Day 12 | Kwong Kau's side questions Choi Tin-fung's financial ability, says Kwong Kau did business in Hainan, owned luxury cars and half share of Kowloon Tong property
Choi Tin-fung case, Day 11 | Defence cross-examination; Choi's mother admits yesterday's claim of owning property was "a mistake"; Kwong Kau's side says she fabricated testimony as she gave it

Choi Tin-fung's mother Cheung Yin-fa today continued to be cross-examined by Kwong Kong-chi's defence, and was twice accused of tailoring her testimony. (File photo)

The case held an in-camera hearing last Friday, closed to the public. Temporary judge Ki Yin-fai told the jury that a legal issue had arisen requiring time to handle and make a ruling, and asked the jury to leave, returning to court only on Monday. When court opened this morning, the judge apologised to the jury and Choi's mother Yin-fa, saying the trial could continue today.

Barrister An Wah-fai, representing Kwong Kong-chi, continued cross-examining Choi Tin-fung's mother Cheung Yin-fa. He asked whether Kwong Kong-chi had used violence against Choi Tin-fung. The mother said "normally before, no"; regarding threats of violence, she said there were after June 2022, and she had heard Choi talking on the phone with Kwong Kong-chi, with Kwong saying "not allowed to sell the property," and the two "argued all the time."

The defence said Kwong Kong-chi never opposed the sale of the Kowloon Tong property. The mother said "at first he did oppose, later it wasn't his call to make." The defence further said Choi Tin-fung persuaded Kwong Kong-chi to bring Kwong Kau to sign a power of attorney. The mother reiterated that initially the whole family disagreed to sell. The defence said they had the right to object. The mother immediately said: "Why is it his call? He never put in any money," and said it was after she told Kwong Kong-chi on the phone "see you in court" that he brought Kwong Kau to sign.

Choi's mother once received about HK$370,000 from Kwong Kong-chi　Said it was from selling a car and other items on the mainland

The defence continued to display conversations between Choi's mother and Choi Tin-fung from October 2022 to January 2023, in which the mother mentioned "last night Alex transferred this amount, HK$370,370." The defence said this was Kwong Kong-chi giving money to the mother to repay gambling debts. The mother denied it: "No, no, no, no, impossible, does he have money to give me? Impossible," saying "he never could have helped me repay money, everything he bought I paid for," "he always used (Choi's) sister's money, how can he tell such lies," and said the funds in question came from selling a car and Hainan property on the mainland.

The defence said Choi's mother did not know if Kwong's mainland business was successful, and that she tailored her testimony to match the prosecution. The mother said: "I never tailored anything, don't you dare wrong me like this." The defence further said she did not know if Kwong made money on the mainland. The mother immediately said "that's complete nonsense," saying she had also gone to the mainland to see for herself, "I know he did nothing, taking my money to squander!"

The defence further said Choi's mother had mentioned that Choi Tin-fung was smart and good at business, but also said Choi put HK$70 million into "a black hole," meaning giving it to Kwong Kong-chi. The mother said the more than HK$70 million was known to the whole Kwong family, "not a single cent was ever recovered." The defence continued to challenge, saying this business didn't seem to be going well, and that the mother's account was only speculation. The mother emphatically denied this, saying she spoke with Kwong almost daily: "Stop blowing his own trumpet, he has nothing, everything was money my daughter gave him!"

Regarding the mother having told her daughter, "today I owe him HK$150,000, but he has also given a lot to mom, and mom sees this," the mother explained that this was scolding Kwong Kong-chi, saying "my daughter gave so much, I helped her look after the kids for 7 or 8 years, he didn't even say thank you." The defence asked why the mother said she owed Kwong HK$150,000. The mother said it was because Kwong bought things for her, and said "I bought so much for him, I never counted, never counted all these years," "said he has no conscience." The defence followed up, asking why the mother said "he has given a lot to mom, and mom sees this," and the mother said "impossible, this really won't happen, he hasn't given me even one cent."

Barrister An Wah-fai, representing Kwong Kong-chi, continued cross-examining Choi's mother today, repeatedly accusing her of gambling and owing debts. (File photo)

The defence says Kwong Kong-chi brought his father to sign a power of attorney　Accuses Choi's mother of tailoring her testimony

Regarding the mother having told her daughter that she mentioned to Kwong Kong-chi about writing a power of attorney, and said if Kwong was sincere he would contact his father and go to the lawyer's office. She explained in court that she told Kwong, "it's easy for you to take your old man to Mong Kok to do a power of attorney," and that Kwong Kau "had no rights at all, just a figurehead." The defence said Kwong ultimately listened to her and brought Kwong Kau to sign the power of attorney. The mother said her daughter had told Kwong Kong-chi to sell, but he refused, "I scolded him and only then he agreed," "I said I've treated you so well all these years, do things with a conscience, if it's like this we'll fall out."

The defence reiterated that Kwong Kong-chi had persuaded Kwong Kau to sign a power of attorney to sell the property. Cheung looked toward the dock and said: "To be honest, if he really had that sincerity, we wouldn't have to meet in this courtroom today." The defence again accused the mother of tailoring her testimony to match the prosecution. She angrily replied: "Don't you dare wrong me, what do you mean by tailoring! Cooperating with the police investigation, what do you mean by tailoring!" saying the Kwong family refused to sell the property from beginning to end. The defence said she didn't know what happened between Choi Tin-fung and Kwong Kong-chi regarding the property sale. The mother admitted she didn't know their communications, but reiterated that as far as she knew the Kwong family refused to sell the car or the property.

Accusation that Choi's mother owed debts; private car splashed with red paint

The defence further pursued the gambling debt issue, saying Choi Tin-fung was unwilling to add the Kowloon Tong property under the mother's name because she had gambling debts. She denied it: "This didn't happen, absolutely didn't happen"; she also denied that Choi sub-mortgaged the Manhattan Hill property to repay her debts. The defence further said Kwong Kong-chi also helped repay her debts. She looked at the dock emotionally and said: "Wow! You came to my home at 15, dating, having children, marrying, divorcing, I treated you like my own son, you helped me repay gambling debts, feel your conscience, you beast, you helped me repay gambling debts, how can you say such things!" Kwong Kong-chi remained expressionless. The defence said the mother's answer was no. The mother said: "There's no such thing! Smear!" When the defence said she gambled or had gambling debts, she also said "how could I," "I just play mahjong sometimes, not all the time."

The defence continued to show photos, saying one of the mother's private cars had been splashed with red paint by debt collectors. The mother confirmed she had reported to the police, saying she was "being framed," wronged, smeared, "the police found nothing... didn't say who it was over," "that person was also arrested, they said they didn't know what was going on," and again said "the beast (Kwong Kong-chi), blames me for everything."

The defence asked who was wronging her. The mother said: "Even my daughter couldn't guard against everything, people want to destroy me, how would I know, I can't control others, but the police investigated and no one came forward saying I owed them money," the defence suggested it might be someone from Macau or the mainland. The mother emotionally said: "You're a lawyer, how can you say 'might, might,' everything needs evidence, if I owed someone money, someone would definitely come forward to claim it!" reiterating "I'm being targeted," and after the investigation they found "I never owed anyone money."

The defence said Choi's mother had reported her private car being splashed with red paint, questioning whether it was due to her gambling debts. The mother denied it. (File photo)

The defence further quoted a message the mother sent her daughter: "Mom owes you, I can never repay it in this lifetime, whatever you want to eat, whatever you ask mom to buy, mom will buy it for you," "this kind of eating is trivial... as long as you want to eat, I can never repay you in this lifetime." The defence said the conversation was related to Choi Tin-fung repaying her gambling debts. The mother disagreed, saying "whatever my daughter asks me to buy, I buy it, mother and daughter don't count these things."

The defence also quoted the mother telling her daughter that she sometimes played mahjong until dawn, "day and night," and couldn't reply in time, expressing gratitude to her daughter. The defence asked if the mother gambled. She didn't consider it gambling, saying playing mahjong was "entertainment," and asked "my daughter was harmed, what's that got to do with me playing mahjong?" The judge asked if money was involved. The mother said "it's very small," meaning "HK$100,000 or HK$80,000 per session." The defence suggested if she played twice a week, she would lose HK$160,000. The mother said "mahjong has wins and losses, how can you lose every day?"

The defence continued, saying the mother lost a lot of money, worrying her daughter. The mother denied it, saying she played mahjong when her daughter was little too, not just now; the defence further said her daughter often repaid her gambling debts. She denied it again: "No such thing, everything needs evidence, my daughter never transferred even HK$10,000 into my account." The defence said the daughter paid the creditors directly. The mother denied it. The defence further said it was Kwong Kong-chi who paid. Cheung angrily said: "No, this beast from the Kwong family, impossible, wow! You help me repay debts, he doesn't know how much he'd have to repay me, spending like this all these years!" murmuring: "These things can be said, truly a demon."

The defence says Kwong Kong-chi was unhappy about police report because he was wanted

The defence also asked about the mother's phone call with Kwong Kong-chi on the day her daughter went missing, saying Kwong was unhappy she reported to the police because he was being wanted. The mother said she called Kwong Kong-chi about twice after reporting to the police, but denied knowing he was wanted, saying Kwong "said it was handled before." The defence asked if the mother asked Kwong why he didn't return to the mainland. She said "why would I ask him whether he returns to the mainland, what's it got to do with me."

The defence further asked whether the mother knew about her daughter and Kwong Kong-chi's investment arrangements on the mainland. The mother said "how much money was given, my daughter told me," and that an agreement was signed such that profits would be split half to the eldest grandson, half for living expenses. The defence said Kwong had connections with watch company Richard Mille in Macau. The mother said she didn't know, "anyway nothing made any money that came back"; but knew her daughter bought watches with Kwong at "Noble Watches," reiterating "my daughter told me, not a single cent came back." The defence said the mother didn't know if her daughter would not tell her about her business because of her gambling debts. The mother disagreed. The defence further said that every time her daughter mentioned large sums of money, the mother would ask her to repay debts, and she might not want to tell her. The mother immediately said Kwong "never made a single cent, he admitted he never made money, and now you're asking these things," denying the defence's suggestion that he might have helped her daughter.

The defence further mentioned that Kwong Kong-chi owned a restaurant called "Teng" (phonetic) on the mainland. The mother said she didn't know, but knew his business partner "Lin Mei-ling" (phonetic), saying "Teng belongs to Sister Ling." The defence asked if she had taken friends to the restaurant to gamble. The mother said it was for meals, "just played once or twice," playing mahjong with chips. As for Kwong introducing gamblers to casinos in Macau, she said she never knew, and never introduced friends to Kwong, saying "Alex stop bragging." The defence also said she didn't know if Kwong gave money to the children. She retorted "no, never," saying she paid to raise her grandchildren from age one to eight, and all the appliances in the Kwong family home were bought by her.

As for the HK$370,000 given by Kwong Kong-chi, the mother explained it was not remitted to her personally, but after selling the car to Sister Ling for about HK$370,000, Kwong Kong-chi remitted it to Hong Kong, and her daughter received it and told her. Regarding the defence's claim that Kwong Kong-chi regularly remitted money to his family, her, and her daughter, the mother said: "Wow, such lies can be told, are you even human? Still telling these lies." The judge said the defence was just presenting its case, no need to attack the lawyer. The mother said "he tells nothing but lies."

The defence further said Kwong had invested in real estate on the mainland. The mother didn't know; the defence further said Kwong gave the mother HK$6 million through Noble Watches, and later remitted HK$1.5 million. The mother said "no such thing," "this money wasn't from Alex to me, I remitted money to him." She also denied the defence's claim that the biggest dispute between Choi Tin-fung and Kwong Kau in February 2023 was about the grandson, reiterating it was over the sale of the Kowloon Tong property, and said since the sale of the Hainan property, Choi Tin-fung "didn't bother with him." Defence cross-examination concluded.

Prosecutor Kwok Sha-lok pointed out that the defence questioned whether Choi's mother had over HK$1 million in monthly living expenses, asking about the value of her clothing and accessories, such as the Hermès Birkin bag she carried last week. The mother said it was worth about HK$100,000-plus. (File photo)

Prosecution re-examines the mother on the value of her clothing and accessories　

Prosecutor Kwok Sha-lok then conducted re-examination. On when the mother learned of her daughter's death, she said she learned from the news, and the police also informed her of her daughter's body condition, describing the moment of learning her daughter "was gone," "my mind went blank," "I can't describe what I was like at the time, couldn't eat, couldn't sleep." Regarding her private car being splashed with red paint, the mother confirmed that from the time of the incident to the trial, an officer called "Sir Ko" had been in continuous contact with her, and the red paint incident happened in February this year. She sent the photos to Sir Ko, hoping the police would "restore my innocence." The case was handled by another police team, who arrested the person involved.

As for the Kwong Kong-chi side having asked whether the mother relied on Kwong Kong-chi to urge Kwong Kau to sell the property. A recording of the mother-daughter conversation was played in court, in which the mother mentioned: "The two kids aren't like him (Kwong Kong-chi), the eldest needs to pay school fees every month... doesn't that cost money?" "Wants to keep everything, doesn't want to sell anything," saying Kwong Kong-chi and Kwong Kau refused to sell the Hainan property and cars, and refused to sign to sell the property. A Hainan dialect recording of Choi Tin-fung was also played. The mother said she said "these thieves have spent so much money over the years, the Hainan house, the Kowloon Tong property, if we can't get them back, we must go through legal proceedings." As for Choi's estate, the mother confirmed that the Manhattan Hill property was sold last year for HK$38 million, used to repay her daughter's mortgage, with the balance used for investment; two parking spaces were sold for HK$2.4 million and HK$1.2 million respectively.

The defence previously questioned the mother's claim that her husband gave her over HK$1 million in monthly living expenses. Kwok Sha-lok re-examined by asking whether the mother spent money on herself, and asked one by one about the prices of her handbags and accessories. The mother showed the black handbag she brought today, saying "these are only a few tens of thousands," about HK$50,000; as for the Hermès Birkin bag she used last week, worth about HK$100,000-plus, "Alex helped me buy that, I paid for it."

As for the watch she wore last week, with diamonds and rubies, the mother said her daughter gave it to her, "a daughter giving things, whether real or fake I'm happy." The diamond bracelets on both wrists, necklace, and earrings are all real diamonds. She said the gold bracelet and necklace were bought many years ago, "these are very old," worth about HK$200,000 to HK$300,000 respectively, the earrings also about HK$100,000-plus. The diamond ring on her hand is about "4-odd carats," and the watch is Piaget brand. She said "real, everything is real, no fakes." After completing her testimony, Choi's mother left by car.

Prosecution calls police officer to testify　Cites Choi's mother saying red paint incident involved money dispute from many years ago

The prosecution later called detective Ko Yan-ki, the main investigator in the Choi Tin-fung case, to testify. He confirmed that in February this year, Choi's mother sent him photos of her vehicle being splashed with red paint, saying he believed she was seeking police assistance. After receiving them, he informed his supervisor, and the criminal damage case was referred to another team to follow up, but he didn't know if any arrests were made. Ko also said he had asked the mother about the reason for the red paint incident. She said it was a "monetary dispute with another woman, but something from many years ago." He didn't remember if it was related to mahjong debts.

Ko reviewed his conversation with Choi's mother in February this year. The mother had mentioned in a recording that the woman often played mahjong at a "bamboo house," and that they used to be good friends, that woman often came to her home for meals. The past was "mahjong debts," "today I win against her, she owes me, tomorrow she wins against me, we can settle later," the two had agreed seven years ago that "we don't owe each other," but later she received threatening phone calls.

Additionally, on the first day of testimony, the mother explained that the Kowloon Tong property was not registered under her name because she held a Whampoa Garden property. Ko said after that day's hearing he was instructed to conduct property searches on the relevant properties.

The case continues tomorrow, with Ko Yan-ki continuing his testimony.

倫敦（美聯社）——喜劇演員羅素·布蘭德（Russell Brand）周一抵達倫敦一間法院，出席其涉嫌強姦及性侵犯指控審訊的首日聆訊。

布蘭德抵達南華克刑事法庭（Southwark Crown Court）時，身邊有保安護衛，並由其妻子Laura Gallacher陪同，案件預計審訊10至12週。

51歲的布蘭德否認三項強姦罪、三項性侵犯罪及一項猥褻侵犯罪。

該等罪行涉及六名女子，據稱發生於1999年至2009年間。

他在審訊前一直准予保釋候審。

控方在早前聆訊中指出，布蘭德被指控在一個工黨黨大會期間於酒店房內強姦一名女子、抓住一名電視台女工作人員的胸部並強迫她在廁所內進行性行為，以及親吻並撫摸一名電台女工作人員。

布蘭德以大膽露骨的單人棟篤笑表演及曾經濫藥和酗酒聞名，是2000年代初期的當紅明星，曾主持電視節目、擁有自己嘅BBC電台節目，並出演過《情迷茱麗葉》（Forgetting Sarah Marshall）和《走佬vana任務》（Get Him to the Greek）等電影。

Apple 正在研發第二代 iPhone Air，而新機有望解決現有型號嘅幾項主要限制。以下係我哋所知道關於 iPhone Air 2 嘅一切資料，包括功能、發佈日期等等。

會否有 iPhone Air 2？

據報導，iPhone Air 嘅銷情比 Apple 預期遜色。《The Information》喺 11 月報導，由於銷量未如預期，Apple 已無限期押後推出第二代型號。

據報 Apple「已通知工程師及供應商，將下一代 iPhone Air 從生產日程中撤走，但未有提供新嘅發佈日期。」

然而喺其後不久，《The Information》更新咗報道，指 Apple 並非完全取消 iPhone Air 2，呢部機仍然積極開發中。

iPhone Air 2 功能

第二個鏡頭

超薄 iPhone Air 設計嘅最大取捨之一，係佢只有一個鏡頭。據報 Apple 正致力為 iPhone Air 2 改變呢一點。

據 Bloomberg 及《The Information》等消息來源指出，iPhone Air 2 將會喺機背加入第二個鏡頭。

Bloomberg 表示，新鏡頭將會係超廣角鏡頭，而唔係遠攝鏡頭。咁會同 Apple 嘅基本型號 iPhone 看齊，後者同樣配備主鏡頭及超廣角鏡頭。

A20 Pro 晶片

據報 iPhone Air 2 將搭載 A20 Pro 處理器，相比現有型號採用嘅 A19 Pro 有所提升。

A20 Pro 晶片將會係 Apple 首款採用 2 納米製程嘅 iPhone 處理器。新嘅製程令 A20 Pro 喺相近晶片尺寸下，提供更強效能及更高能源效益。

該晶片亦會採用另一項名為晶圓級多晶片模組（Wafer-Level Multi-Chip Module）嘅新技術，喺晶圓層面將 SoC 同 DRAM 整合，從而提升效能並降低功耗。

更長嘅電池續航

據報 Apple 亦正致力提升 iPhone Air 2 嘅電池續航。

根據供應鏈爆料，iPhone Air 2 將配備 3,500mAh 電池。作為比較，第一代 iPhone Air 嘅電池容量為 3,149mAh，即新機電池容量增加咗超過一成。

除咗加大電池嘅實際容量之外，憑藉 A20 Pro 晶片嘅效率提升，iPhone Air 2 嘅續航亦有望更長。

不過要留意嘅係，iPhone 嘅電池續航受好多因素影響，要等 Apple 正式發表 iPhone Air 2 先知確實嘅續航數字。

均溫板

據《The Information》報導，iPhone Air 2 將配備均溫板散熱系統。Apple 早前喺 iPhone 17 Pro 首度採用均溫板散熱技術，強調散熱效能及性能均有顯著提升。

如果 Apple 將均溫板引入 iPhone Air 2，意味住裝置喺高負載工作時能保持較低溫度，並能更長時間維持高效能表現。

iPhone Air 2：發佈日期

iPhone Air 2 原定預計於 2026 年 9 月，與 iPhone 18 Pro 系列同步發表。

不過 Bloomberg 最近報導，Apple 計劃喺 2027 年春季，與新嘅基本型號 iPhone 18 同步推出 iPhone Air 2。

你點睇 Apple 對 iPhone Air 2 嘅規劃？Apple 嘅改動同改良係咪正確？欢迎喺留言區告訴我哋。

我嘅心水 iPhone 配件：

  • 內置螢幕嘅 Anker Nano USB-C 牆充
  • AirPods Pro 3：查看目前特價
  • 同時為你所有 Apple 裝置充電
  • 為任何汽車加入無線 CarPlay
  • 可顯示充電速度嘅 USB-C 線

追蹤 Chance：Threads、Bluesky、Instagram 及 Mastodon。

{'text': '邊個話而家所有私隱保障都一定要係數碼嘅？以我嘅工作性質，出差好常見，喺咖啡店、火車或者酒店大堂工作對我嚟講係家常便飯。所以當我偶然發現呢個識得喺你移開視線嘅一瞬間將屏幕模糊化嘅精巧私隱應用程式時，我就即刻被吸引住。', 'paragraph_context': 'Who said all privacy protections had to be digital nowadays? In my line of work, traveling can be common, and working from a coffee shop, train, or hotel lounge is something I do on the regular. So when I came across this nifty privacy app that knows to blur your screen the second you look away, I was enthralled.'}

{'text': '呢個應用程式叫做 ShyGlass，由開發者 Max Rovensky 開發。佢上個月喺 X 上面發布咗一段 10 秒嘅示範短片，至今已累積超過 23 萬次觀看。運作方式相當簡單：佩戴 AirPods 期間，如果你將頭部轉去某個角度，你嘅 MacBook 屏幕就會變模糊；當你將頭部轉返去，屏幕就會自動恢復清晰。', 'paragraph_context': 'The app is called ShyGlass, and it comes from developer Max Rovensky, who posted a 10-second demo on X last month that has since racked up over 230,000 views. The way it works is pretty simple. While wearing a pair of AirPods, if you turn your head to a certain degree, your MacBook screen blurs. When you turn your head back, the screen unblurs itself.'}

{'text': '喺背後運作嘅，係 Apple 用喺空間音訊動態頭部追蹤嘅動態感應器——即係當你轉頭時令你嘅音樂保持定點嘅功能。ShyGlass 用嘅係同一組動態數據，但目的係偵測用戶嘅在場狀態。用戶可以從選單列校準一個中央位置，而每當頭部偏離設定角度（預設為 15 度，可調整範圍由 2 度到 30 度），屏幕就會逐漸變模糊，直至完全遮蓋。', 'paragraph_context': 'Behind the scenes, it’s using the motion sensors Apple uses for dynamic head tracking in Spatial Audio, the feature that keeps your music anchored when you look around. ShyGlass uses the same motion data but to detect presence. A user calibrates a center position from the menu bar, and anytime head positioning drifts past a set angle (15° by default, adjustable from 2° to 30°), a blur fades in over the display until it’s fully covered.'}

{'text': '畢竟呢度係 Security Bite，所以我想就呢個程式需要嘅權限分享幾個想法：屏幕錄製。ShyGlass 確實需要擷取用戶屏幕嘅快照以套用模糊效果，聽落對一個私隱工具嚟講有啲諷刺。根據開發者所講，快照只會留喺記憶體中，唔會儲存或上傳，而且擷取動作會喺模糊效果停止嘅同一刻停止。', 'paragraph_context': 'Now this is Security Bite after all, so I have a couple of thoughts on the permission the app needs: Screen Recording. ShyGlass does need to pull a snapshot of a user’s display to apply the blur effect, which kind of sounds a little ironic for a privacy tool. According to the developer, the snapshot stays in memory and is never saved or uploaded, and capture stops the moment the blur does.'}

{'text': '我冇理由懷疑呢番說話。但呢度嘅取捨值得拎出嚟講。屏幕錄製係 Mac 上最強大嘅權限之一。擁有呢個權限嘅應用程式可以無時無刻睇到你睇緊嘅所有嘢，而 macOS 冇辦法強制執行應用程式「只喺佢聲稱嘅時候」先擷取畫面。所以基本上你只能選擇相信開發者嘅承諾。', 'paragraph_context': 'I have no reason to doubt that. But it’s worth bring up the trade here. Screen Recording is one of the most powerful permissions on the Mac. An app with it can see everything you see, all the time, and macOS has no way of enforcing that it only looks when it says it does. So you’re basically taking the developer at his word.'}

{'text': '不過，我覺得佢嘅用途大多數時候都好實用。例如喺飛機上轉過身同隔籬位嘅人傾偈，又或者喺公眾場所翻你個袋。每當你嘅頭離開屏幕，總會有一刻其他人嘅目光可能會落到你嘅工作內容上。', 'paragraph_context': 'Still, I find its functionality useful more often than not. Like turning to chat with the person next to you on a flight, or digging through your bag in a public space. Any time your head leaves the screen, there’s a window where someone else’s eyes can land on whatever you’re working on.'}

翁子光新作《超風》講述跨性別人士追求蛻變過程，電影取名自金庸筆下「梅超風」一角 — 雌雄渾然一體、愛得徹底、痛得轟烈。戲中部份情節藍本，源於編劇李嘉怡（Annabelle）親身經歷。

「我會話，我嘅故事係唔獨特嘅」。30 年性別掙扎、時想「轉換角色」的蠢蠢欲動和罪惡感、同學側目、家人不解，「出櫃」換來父親斷絕聯繫，更明言禁她出席喪禮。這位「城中俠女」如斯自述，為的是性小眾能在電影和她的故事中，見自己，同呼吸，在傷痕添上一抹色彩和希望。

「如果我十幾年前去睇呢套戲，我應該會再早啲有咁嘅勇氣（開展跨性別過程）」。

《超風》講述跨性別女性「超風」，從內地來港，希望賺錢完成性別肯定手術，成為真正的自己，途中遇上癮君子男友的愛與糾纏，以及與知己小梅的靈魂共震，令超風反思真正自由的模樣。

在故事成形前，翁子光團隊就跨性別社群作田野研究，找上了跨性別組織「跨青時刻」，表明希望邀請一位跨女受訪，而 Annabelle 當時正是該組織的委員，時常為社群進行倡議工作。

他們一行數人在酒吧聊起來，Annabelle 起初有所擔憂，要求團隊不可公開她樣貌、故事細節等，但這些拘謹隨著聊天過程慢慢放鬆，「佢哋問到好仔細，我嘅愛情生活係點樣、食藥前食藥後，心理上有咩分別，所以我覺得佢哋係想寫到一個好立體、好真實嘅曲線出嚟，個信任就喺嗰度」，一聊就是六小時。

半年後，翁子光開拍前相約她再見面，問她對劇本意見，邀請她任《超風》編劇，成為她首次參與電影創作的作品。

「如果我要寫一個我人生故事嘅電影版本，佢（《超風》）好多地方都好似，其實呢個就係我嘅人生」。

美少女戰士的掙扎

電影不時穿插超風小時候片段，兩個小孩在扮演武俠片一男一女，生理性別為男生的超風，被安排扮演男角，他卻凝視著女角吐出一句：「我想換角色」。Annabelle 五歲時已有如斯感覺。她記得，每天放學後，就愛買一支唧唧冰，然後跑回家看卡通。當時《叮噹》和《美少女戰士》隔天播放，「我特別鍾意美少女戰士，成日都會幻想『啊，呢個好靚』」。那年生日，餅店放著叮噹和美少女戰士的蛋糕，一股掙扎湧動開始出現。

「我嗰時已經有種 shame（羞恥）喺度，即係我作為一個男士，係唔應該揀美少女戰士」。

Annabelle 這種拉扯，來自中學，她試盡一切性別流動的舉措，留長髮、玩搖滾樂、塗指甲油，「中學嘅時候，我已經同朋友講過『我覺得我係一個女人』」。後來到美國升讀大學，礙於他人歧視目光，只好繼續飾演一個男生。

「You are like a bi*ch」

長期壓抑，令 Annabelle 20 歲時向家人「出櫃」，父母離異，她先向較能接受的媽媽剖白。媽媽不知解何謂跨性別，「佢聽唔明，佢就問『其實你係咪 Gay（男同性戀）？即係你係 Gay』」。Annabelle 起初花費唇舌解釋，慢慢變成不悅，「其實我係好嬲，同埋好傷心，我根本唔知點樣同佢解釋，因為我好希望我一講佢就明白我，我好需要一個人去同我講『OK，我知道你做緊咩』」。

「出櫃」後，家人的關係變得奇差，一年只見面兩、三次，Annabelle 亦不會再吐心聲，「嗰時我媽形容我好似箭豬，你一梳我啲毛梳錯方向，我就會起弶，所以我覺得佢（媽媽）都會好擔心講錯嘢，唔知我個心諗緊咩」。

要向父親「出櫃」更難，「我會話佢係一個好有邏輯嘅人，亦都因為佢覺得自己好聰明，佢一覺得自己係啱，係成個世界都說服唔到」。30 歲，Annabelle 打算開展跨性別過程，向爸爸坦白。同樣不理解，但爸爸起初的反應是無比溫暖，「佢就話，仔定女我唔理喇，你都係我嘅寶貝」。

然而，隨著父親了解跨性別之義，這抹溫暖變成恨的火焰，「佢越睇越多，就同我講『我覺得呢件事係病』、『呢個決定係你人生最差嘅一個決定』」。半年間，Annabelle 每次與他談及跨性別，都是以淚流滿面收場。終於有一次，她禁不住大吵一場，換來爸爸一句：「You are like a bi*ch, like your mom（你就像一個婊子，像你媽媽一樣）」，自此兩人分道揚鑣。

被拒出席喪禮後的一句「Thank you」

戲中超風因父親得重病，趕回鄉見其最後一面，出門前超風束起長髮、紮起胸部、卸下妝容，一點點抹去自己的身份。Annabelle 有著相同的經歷。在與父親斷絕聯繫後半年，她收到家人通知父親患上末期癌症，於是主動聯絡他。

「我就寫話『想見你啦』，覺得有個好嚟好去，但佢覆我『你唔好再聯絡我』」。在父親住院至離世的一個月，他亦多次向親戚表明，不願讓 Annabelle 參加他的喪禮、甚至看到他的最後一面。「所以其實我無咗一個好實質嘅感覺，係我可以放低呢啲好複雜嘅感情，然後畀佢過去，我無一個咁樣嘅地方」。

父親喪禮當天，Annabelle 如超風一樣，將自己女生的狀態隱藏，「我出去之前我諗咗好多，我唔想屋企人見到最真實嘅我」。她站在火葬場外，沒有見最後一面、沒有道別，只帶著「男兒身」看著炊煙縈繞。

事後，Annabelle 一位姑姐走到她跟前，說了一聲「Thank you（謝謝）」，「我係好嬲，想一拳車落去，佢多謝我咩呢？我覺得佢多謝緊我一個被抹退嘅感覺，話你咁樣犧牲自己係好高尚、好有道德性嘅嘢，所以我好嬲」。

成為觀眾的「小梅」

Apple 將於本月底推出全新的 M6 MacBook Pro，配備 14 吋屏幕，沿用現有的工業設計。憑藉 M6 晶片，這部新 MacBook Pro 有三項值得期待的升級。

#1：雙 16 核心神經網絡引擎

如果 AI 對你的工作流程有任何重要性——而隨著 macOS 27 的 AI 功能推出，這對更多用戶而言將會是事實——那麼 M6 MacBook Pro 可能是一項重大升級。

這是因為 M6 晶片配備了雙 16 核心神經網絡引擎，比 M5 及之前型號的標準 16 核心版本更強。Apple 表示：

M6 同時引入雙 16 核心神經網絡引擎，提供比前代高出達 2 倍的峰值運算能力，讓裝置上的 AI 工作流程運行得更快。系統框架可自動同時運用兩個引擎，使應用程式獲得更快的模型執行速度。

#2：配備強大新核心的 12 核心 CPU 及 GPU

基本版 M6 晶片配備 12 核心 CPU 及 12 核心 GPU。兩者都是對 M5 的大幅升級，後者僅有 10 核心。

M6 的 CPU 核心特別值得留意，因為 Apple 首次在其基本版晶片中引入三種不同的核心類型。當中包括 2 個超級核心、4 個性能核心，以及 6 個節能核心。以下是 Apple 對每種核心的介紹：

  • 超級核心：「瞬間完成單線程工作負載」
  • 性能核心：「耗電更低，並與超級核心協作運行高需求的多線程工作負載」
  • 節能核心：「處理日常背景任務」

以往只有 M5 Pro、M5 Max 及 M5 Ultra 能在單一晶片中同時提供超級核心與性能核心。但現在這些 Pro 級功能已可供標準版 M6 用戶享用。

Epic Games 指控 Apple「製造」了一場關於其新建議 App Store 抽成比率法律程序嘅暫停。Apple 並不同意。以下係詳細內容。

在一份聯合進度更新中，Epic Games 同 Apple 對 Apple 交出內部文件以解釋點樣得出新建議 App Store 抽成比率嘅努力，給出咗截然唔同嘅說法。

少少背景

提一提大家，今年八月，Apple 為透過外部 App Store 連結所進行嘅購買，建議咗一套新嘅抽成結構。

根據建議嘅結構，開發者需支付嘅抽成將由 5% 至 15% 不等，相比 Apple 在 2024 年引入嘅 27% 費用有所下降；嗰個 27% 嘅收費係喺法院命令 Apple 必須允許開發者引導用戶使用其他支付方式之後推出嘅。

法院其後裁定 Apple 違反咗該命令，Apple 而家正喺最高法院尋求推翻呢個裁定，辯稱該命令從未禁止佢收取任何抽成。

喺最高法院考慮 Apple 對藐視裁決嘅上訴期間，另一間下級法院正另行審視 Apple 能否對透過外部連結進行嘅購買收取抽成，以及如果可以嘅話可以收幾多。

Apple 近期曾試圖暫停嗰啲程序，等最高法院先作裁決，但佢嘅請求接連被下級法院同最高法院拒絕。

作為程序一部分，Apple 喺八月提交咗佢建議嘅 5% 至 15% 抽成結構，同埋支持呢啲比率嘅證據。

根據規管呢啲程序嘅協議，Apple 仲被要求交出內部文件，顯示佢係點樣得出呢啲比率。

呢啲文件旨在畀 Epic 一個機會，喺正式回應法院之前，審視 Apple 建議費用嘅基礎。

最新嘅爭議就係喺呢度出現：Epic 指控 Apple 蓄意拖延程序，Apple 則否認呢啲指控。

Apple 同 Epic 對新建議 App Store 費用背後嘅證據各執一詞

喺聯合進度文件入面，Epic 表示：「距離其提交文件嘅期限差不多兩個月，Apple 幾乎未有交出任何文件」，並補充指「Apple 一再唔願意承諾一個確實日期完成文件提交，呢一點表明法院介入係必須嘅。」

Apple 否認呢啲指控，辯稱佢已經履行咗初步責任，交出咗解釋點樣得出新建議比率嘅文件。

該公司仲將拖延嘅責任推畀 Epic，話《Fortnite》開發商花咗幾星期先提出額外嘅文件要求，之後仲要求涉及 27 名人士嘅廣泛搜尋。Apple 表示已同意呢啲要求，預計可喺 11 月 25 日前大致完成文件提交。

喺文件入面，Epic 亦反駁 Apple 嘅說法，即只有四名高級行政人員參與釐定建議嘅抽成比率，該四名行政人員分別係 Tim Cook、Eddy Cue、Kevan Parekh 同 Carson Oliver。

Epic 認為，呢個決定亦參考咗 Apple 內部其他團隊嘅討論同分析，包括喺美國以外市場就替代抽成結構所做嘅工作。（講到呢一點，亦存在另一爭議，就係 Epic 應唔應該取得涉及 Apple 國際抽成政策嘅文件。）

Apple 則堅稱，決策過程相比當初釐定原本 27% 抽成時要狹窄得多，而且主要依賴外聘專家嘅分析，而唔係更廣泛嘅內部討論。

Apple 表示已提交支撐其建議嘅商業記錄同數據，並反駁 Epic 指必定有更大批員工參與釐定新比率嘅說法。

喺整個反駁 Epic 指控嘅過程中，Apple 一再強調佢已同意 Epic 對額外文件同更廣泛搜尋嘅要求，認為導致延誤嘅係呢啲要求嘅範圍，以及 Epic 提出要求所花嘅時間。

Apple 仲表示，Epic 突然要求法院強制訂立 11 月 1 日為完成文件提交嘅死線，而唔係先同 Apple 商討呢個死線，令佢感到意外。Apple 對 Epic 對其同意提交文件範圍嘅反對亦提出類似論點，話 Epic 應該先直接提出呢啲關注，再尋求法院介入，而非一開始就訴諸法院。

另一方面，Epic 就話：「Apple 對 Epic 提出嘅每個要求都裝作驚訝，就好像各方、本法院、Hixson 法官，以及法院委任嘅三名特別專家，啱啱先完成咗一個長達數月嘅程序，從 Apple 度攞到 Epic 明明有權取得嘅文件。」

因此，Epic 要求法院命令 Apple：

  • 「[即]時開始分批提交文件，並喺合理時間內——且不遲於 2026 年 11 月 1 日——全部完成提交」
  • 「喺上述死線前提交所有相關文件，唔好理 Apple 對其提交範圍所設嘅人為限制，詳情見[文件]。 」

Apple 今日展開一項新推廣活動，宣傳 Safari 比起 Chrome 更具優勢。透過在其網站開設全新的「改用 Safari」（Switch to Safari）專頁，並發布兩條新 YouTube 影片，Apple 欲令所有人都知道 Safari 是「比 Chrome 更強大、更重視私隱的瀏覽器」。

就在 Apple 股價因 iPhone 18 Pro 減產消息而受挫數日後，摩根大通將其 AAPL 目標價調高 20 美元。詳情如下。

iPhone Duo 有助抵銷分階段發售帶來嘅影響

上星期五，《日經亞洲》引述「多名知情人士」報道，Apple 已通知特定供應商調減 iPhone 18 Pro 同 iPhone 18 Pro Max 嘅零部件產量，原因係「需求疲軟」。

該消息拖累 Apple 喺開市早段跌約 2.5%，不過股價其後已收復大部分失地，今日收報 340.97 美元。

話雖如此，摩根大通今日發布新嘅投資者報告（經 AppleInsider 引述），指出相關減產消息同 Apple 嘅一貫生產模式一致，未必代表需求出現意外下滑。

報告亦談及 Apple 分階段推出 iPhone 嘅安排，摩根大通預期 iPhone Duo 可以抵銷因為常規版 iPhone 18 延至明年初開賣所帶來嘅銷售缺口。

有趣嘅係，今日較早時中國《證券時報》另一篇報道指，Apple 已經將 iPhone Duo 嘅訂單增加 30%，令 2026 年餘下時間嘅產量有望接近 1,000 萬部。

展望 12 月份嘅季度，摩根大通預期 Apple 將售出 850 萬部 iPhone Duo。摩根大通亦預計 iPhone 收入按年下跌約 2%，但 Apple 整體收入會上升 2%。

該行亦繼續警示供應限制同更廣泛嘅經濟壓力可能會影響消費者需求。

綜合而言，摩根大通將 AAPL 目標價由 340 美元調高至 360 美元，同時維持對該股嘅「增持」評級。
